_doc: RO4, OP3, OP4 in design/RimMandrake/operating_requirements_2026-11-01.md. Operations owns this table. routes: first match wins, by fnmatch on an ops_watch metric or alarm key, or a Dispatcher alarm kind. route program = the program contained it, the journal holds it, no incident; a program route with a `band` ({min, max}) and a `runbook` line is a repeat alarm a program answers: while its reading is MEASURED in band the runbook line is noted on its item and no Operations run is bought (role_launch.program_answered), and out of band or unread it is a role route for its `reader` and `cause` (incident.program_answer; design/specs/2026-11-19-incident-news-and-program-routes/boundary.md); the band also grades that metric's revisit news (incident.reading_moved); role = an incident for `reader`, rising the chain; owner = an incident that starts at him. cause: readings sharing it are one incident. class: for an alarm with no ranges class. readers: who may be filed for, and what wakes them. breaker_emergency is program because its own told row (relentless.breaker_same_cause) is the signal; dry:* because a dry tick writes nothing and its operator reads the alarm. selftest_incident.py fails on a kind this table misses (alarm_census.py reads them from the source) and `rimflow file --for` refuses a reader not here.

policy._doc: chain[0] is the route's reader. ladder: minutes from told_at to chain[2] and chain[3]; chain[1] comes at the reading's ack_within_min. OP4: emergency reaches him at 60 unacked, distressed after 4 h. min_step_min: at least this long on a rung, which is what spaces the rungs after an expired recover_by. event_quiet_min covers a Dispatcher alarm, a reading with no sane value: 7 h clears the 6 h alarm_every_s rate limit, so a repeat is seen. chain entries asking the reader's own role again are skipped (incident.next_rung; an Operations reader goes Operations, Conductor, him, at chain[3]'s minute; INCIDENT_CHAIN_DEDUPE_OPERATIONS_RUNG). runs_per_hour: the Conductor and fresh Operations runs incidents may ask for, shared by all incidents; the reader's own alarm run is held by the role's alarm_run_gap_s and daily limits. owner_revisit_min: an incident at his rung is revisited (a fresh Operations run re-reads it, its ack and plan cleared) this long after it reached him or was last revisited, or at its recover_by if an ack set a later one (OPS_ROLE_DIAGNOSE_STARVED_AT_FOUR_RUNS). A revisit with no news (readings and plan unchanged since the last one, incident.revisit_news; revisit_clock_slack_min: a clock metric only aged if it rose by the status time elapsed, within this) is re-armed with no run and a revisit_quiet row, for at most revisit_quiet_max_min since a run last read it. revisit_batch_min: a run going out takes every revisit due inside this many minutes, so staggered incidents fall into step (an ack whose recover_by lies past the window is untouched) (measured 2026-11-03: revisits came 2 to 15 min apart, each its own run; INCIDENT_REVISIT_TAME_SAME_NEWS_HOURLY). tame_relapses / tame_window_h: a relapse is a closed incident reopened (inside relapse_h); the tame_relapses-th of one cause inside tame_window_h stops it buying full Operations reads and files one structural item, spawned --from structural_from, quoting its acks; it stays open on its ladder (INCIDENT_RELAPSE_TAME_STOP_FULL_READS; plan-20261101164253 was one relapse, then a join).
policy._deep_read_why: the incident clerk (design/specs/2026-11-19-incident-clerk/boundary.md; owner's card 2026-11-19, "one deep Opus run a day stays"): a plan acked with --trigger is re-read by the program, which rings a run only when the line is crossed or cannot be read, or the rung moves; once a day from this local time every open untamed incident at his rung is re-read by one Operations run on Opus, whatever its line says. 07:00 sits inside cover_window_s of the 07:30 economy slot, so that run covers the slot instead of adding one (role_launch.covered_slot). null: no deep read.

_drainers: incident.receiver_problem (RIMMANDRAKE_FIX_ALARM_RECEIVER_TRUSTS_RETIRED_RELENTLESS_POOL): a live program that works through alarm items filed --for seat --needs needs, and, when tags is set, only alarms of those ops_watch tags.
